subject: Materials Science
title: Skin Substitutes
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Skin Substitutes.

hook.text: A severe burn destroys skin faster than the body can regrow it — engineered skin substitutes fill the gap.

buildup.text: Acellular dermal matrices provide a collagen scaffold — the patient's own cells migrate in and rebuild the dermis.

discovery.text: Living skin equivalents grow fibroblasts in collagen gel topped with keratinocytes — mimicking real skin's two layers.

twist.text: No engineered skin yet includes hair follicles, sweat glands, or nerves — it's a wound cover, not a full organ.

climax.text: Products like Integra and Apligraf have saved thousands of burn patients — buying time for the body to regenerate.

punchline.text: Engineered skin can't replace the real thing — but it keeps patients alive.

quiz.question: What is a current limitation of engineered skin substitutes?
options: They are rejected by all patients
They lack hair follicles, sweat glands, and nerve endings
They are thicker than natural skin
